title: Coarse higher-moment bound for low-degree functions
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\lambda,q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\lambda\le1$ and $2\le q$. Suppose every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$. If every product component of a real-valued function $f$ indexed by a set of size greater than $k$ vanishes identically, then $\|f\|_{q,P}\le\bigl(\sqrt q\,\lambda^{1/q-1/2}\bigr)^k\|f\|_{2,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
Every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$
Every product component of $f$ indexed by a set of size greater than $k$ vanishes at every outcome
$f$ is a real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1$. For $q\ge2$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, $\|f\|_{q,P}\le(\sqrt q\lambda^{1/q-1/2})^k\|f\|_{2,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; degree at most $k$ means $h_S=0$ for every $|S|>k$.
